extracted.intended_audience: IP lawyers, in-house counsel and regulatory teams at pharmaceutical and life sciences companies
extracted.subtask_short: EU unitary SPCs and SPC recast
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and explain the European Commission's April 27, 2023 proposal to introduce unitary Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) and a recast of the SPC Regulation, focusing on impacts for medicinal products and related procedural, eligibility and litigation consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPC basic duration calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: An SPC takes effect at the end of the patent term and remains in force for the period between the date of patent filings and the date that the first marketing authorization (MA) for the medicinal product covered by such patent was granted, minus five years (and subject to a maximum duration of five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how the SPC term is calculated under the current SPC Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 and remains a central eligibility/term metric for SPCs; applicants must check filing and MA dates carefully to compute duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pediatric extension for SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The period may be subject to a possible six-month extension under the Pediatric Regulation 1901/2006/EC upon the successful completion of an agreed pediatric investigation plan (currently only for non-orphan products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where eligible, a 6-month SPC extension applies only if an agreed pediatric investigation plan is completed successfully; determine orphan vs non-orphan status and plan compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current requirement for national SPC filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holders must lodge separate SPC applications with national patent offices in order to obtain SPC protection in each Member State where such protection is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the pre-unitary regime, securing SPC protection across the EU requires multiple national filings, creating administrative burden and costs that the unitary SPC aims to reduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary patent vs national patents (scope and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unitary patent is a single, uniform patent right that will have effect in all Member States participating in the unitary patent system; the corresponding Unified Patent Court (UPC) will provide a forum for uniform patent litigation in participating countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which Member States participate (25 agreed, 17 signed/ratified UPCA to date) to determine the territorial scope of a unitary patent and any attached unitary SPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary SPCs attach to unitary patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary SPC rights will attach to the underlying unitary patent and will therefore take effect in the (currently) 17 Member States that will recognize unitary patents from June 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unitary SPCs are territorially limited to the states recognizing the corresponding unitary patent; eligibility and strategic decisions depend on participating states list and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary SPC availability restricted to centralized-approved medicinal products
rubrics_metrics.description: For medicinal products, unitary SPCs will only be available for products approved via the centralized procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure the MA was granted through the EU centralized authorization procedure to qualify for a unitary SPC for medicinal products.

rubrics_metrics.name: EUIPO as examining and enforcement body for unitary SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) will be the body responsible for examining and issuing unitary SPCs. The EUIPO will also handle third party opposition proceedings and will have jurisdiction to hear revocation actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural route changes: applicants and third parties should expect examination, opposition and revocation processes at EUIPO level rather than national offices for unitary SPCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals path for unitary SPC decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unitary SPC applicants who receive a negative opinion from the EUIPO will be able to appeal the decision before the Boards of Appeal of the EUIPO, with further appeals possible to the Court of Justice of the European Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a defined multi-level appeal route (EUIPO Boards of Appeal → CJEU) for challenging EUIPO decisions on unitary SPCs; factor appeal capacity and timing into enforcement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined application procedure (unitary SPC + national SPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies that satisfy the relevant SPC requirements will be able to file a 'combined application' to obtain both a unitary SPC and a bundle of national SPCs for any Member States not included under the protection of the corresponding unitary patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined application permits a single filing to seek unitary SPC protection where available and national SPCs for other states; evaluate whether combined filing is suitable for territorial strategy and cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on double protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Double protection by both a unitary SPC and a national SPC in any given Member State is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must avoid overlapping unitary and national SPC rights for the same Member State; strategic territorial selections and filing choices must respect the prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation and revocation forum for unitary SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Regulation intends for unitary SPCs to be able to be litigated before the body responsible under national law for the revocation of the corresponding basic patent. Assuming that the Agreement on a Unified Patent Court (UPCA) is updated accordingly, infringements of unitary SPC rights may be handled by the new Unified Patent Court (provided that the Court has relevant jurisdiction over the underlying unitary patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation strategies may involve national revocation forums or the UPC depending on jurisdictional updates; verify how revocation and infringement jurisdiction will be allocated in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recitals clarifications affecting SPC interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed recast includes new explanatory language within the recitals that clarifies issues from prior EU case law, which will likely impact interpretation of SPC rights and eligibility requirements by national patent offices and courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recitals can shape future interpretation; practitioners should track recital wording changes because they may alter eligibility outcomes and national office practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on third-party (hostile) SPCs without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The language in the proposed recitals confirms that an SPC cannot be granted to a patent holder on the basis of an MA held by a third party without such third party’s consent (so called 'third party SPCs' or sometimes 'hostile SPCs').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification directly addresses contentious practices; applicants relying on another party’s MA must secure consent or risk ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple SPCs and therapeutically equivalent derivatives guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is new language regarding the acceptability of having multiple SPCs in connection with a single product, and new explanatory language regarding the SPC protections available for a given product and its therapeutically equivalent derivatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recast seeks to clarify when multiple SPCs may be appropriate and how therapeutically equivalent derivatives are treated, affecting life-cycle planning and generic strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated cost savings from unitary SPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s accompanying factsheet states that the new system will provide estimated savings of €137,000 per applicant that receives five-year-long SPC protection in all 27 Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies potential administrative/cost benefit from moving to unitary SPCs vs separate national SPC filings; use for cost-benefit and filing strategy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to plant protection SPCs (parallel proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of this blog, focus was on SPCs for medicinal products, although similar proposals apply with respect to plant protection SPCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that analogous rules are being proposed for plant protection products; consult the plant-protection-specific provisions when relevant.
